title: Trump ‘quietly shelves plans for business deals with Putin’

The Trump administration has quietly abandoned plans to use business deals to incentivise Vladimir Putin to bring an end to the war in Ukraine after disinterest from the Kremlin, according to a report.

US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff had proposed deals in the energy and aviation sectors as they sought to use business to finally push Moscow to agreeing a peace deal.

They told European officials that these corporate tie-ups were no longer central to Washington’s pitch to Moscow, five officials briefed on the matter told the Financial Times.

Among the moves being discussed by senior Russian and US officials was bringing the US into the Nord Stream pipelines that delivered gas to Germany before Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022.

Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law, also floated postwar ideas such as US companies investing in Russian oil projects and titanium production ventures, the FT said.

Despite apparent initial interest from Moscow, Russian officials have since cooled on the idea, continuing to insist instead that Ukraine give up territory and make other concessions that Kyiv has repeatedly stated are unacceptable, the newspaper added.

"It was made pretty clear that the Russians were not in the market for this kind of thing," one of the officials told the paper.

In October, the Trump administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel that were designed to deprive Moscow of revenue for its ‌war on Ukraine after Russia agreed to supply ​diesel to global markets in an effort to lower fuel prices.

When contacted by the outlet, a US official described the reporting as “not accurate”, adding: “We are organising our negotiating tracks and will announce them when we are ready and this continues to be an element.”

The Independent has contacted the White House for further comment.

The Kremlin is, however, reportedly keen on a US offer to discuss postwar European security.

The proposal to discuss broader security arrangements for Europe was floated by Trump’s envoys last week, but Kyiv and its Western allies fear Russian involvement will play into Moscow’s hands and weaken Nato.

The Kremlin strongly backed the US idea, repeating its long-held position that a new European security framework would be needed to end the conflict. Russia has repeatedly claimed, without evidence, that Nato’s eastern flank represents an existential threat.

Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky wants a ceasefire to include guarantees to ensure that Russia does not attack his country again.

Moscow meanwhile wants the US and its allies make a commitment to not deploy weapons or conduct any military activities in Ukraine and other ex-Soviet nations.
summary: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have abandoned proposed deals in the energy and aviation sectors with Moscow
